basis: Lysosomal storage disorder with defining skeletal dysplasia in 4/4; aortic valve disease in 2/4. Floaters alone do not establish ocular damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: pervasive skeletal dysplasia, including vertebral abnormalities and hip dysplasia in 4/4, defines the clinical phenotype.

basis: Catecholamine-secreting chromaffin tumours; hypertension occurs in 30-79%. Retinopathy, nephropathy and cerebral haemorrhage are separately diagnosed complications.

decisions.neurologic: none: adrenal endocrine tumours predominate across this umbrella; extra-adrenal autonomic tumours are a subset, and cranial nerve compression occurs in 5-29%.

basis: Progressive neurodegeneration and blinding optic atrophy define disease; structural skeletal abnormalities include pes cavus in 3/3 and pectus carinatum in 2/3.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: structural skeletal deformities are common, with pes cavus in 3/3 and pectus carinatum in 2/3; this exceeds motor symptoms alone.

basis: Progressive CNS disorder; muscle-fibre abnormalities in 3/5 and contractures in 5/12 support musculoskeletal involvement. Visual and respiratory impairment may be neurogenic.

decisions.ocular: none: visual impairment in 8/12 does not localize damage to the eye or optic nerve; cerebral visual impairment remains possible.

basis: Eye-origin lymphoid malignancy; direct CNS lymphoma involvement develops in roughly 50-80% of the predominant vitreoretinal form during its course.

decisions.neurologic: involved: CNS infiltration by the same lymphoma occurs in approximately 50-80% of primary vitreoretinal cases over the typical course.

basis: Microcephaly, intellectual disability, syndactyly and digital malformations define syndrome; cutaneous fusion is a defining skin lesion. Optic atrophy occurs in 30-79%.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: cutaneous syndactyly is explicitly a defining feature; frequent nail hypoplasia provides additional skin-appendage evidence.

basis: Cardiac malformation and extensive skeletal dysplasia characterize the syndrome. Intellectual disability and ocular findings lack established frequencies or diagnostic status.

decisions.neurologic: none: intellectual disability and microcephaly are listed without frequencies; the supplied evidence does not establish either as a major diagnostic criterion or a >=30% feature.

basis: Peroxisomal metabolic defect defined by adult cognitive decline, seizures and neuropathy; pigmentary retinopathy occurs in 1/2 reported patients. Infantile liver disease is rare.

decisions.neurologic: primary: adult cognitive decline, seizures and sensorimotor neuropathy explicitly characterize the disease in its definition.

basis: Distal osteolysis and intellectual disability define the named syndrome; dental abnormalities occur in 80-99%. Proptosis alone does not establish ocular damage.

decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability is part of the explicit syndrome synonyms and definition, supported by an 80-99% HPO frequency.

basis: Named syndrome combines cerebral calcifications, abnormal teeth and renal phosphate wasting. No definition establishes systemic phosphate depletion or another metabolic disorder.

decisions.renal: primary: pathological phosphaturia identifies renal phosphate wasting as a defining component of the named syndrome.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: phosphaturia alone does not establish systemic hypophosphataemia or an independent metabolic disorder; renal phosphate loss is already represented.
